q: Who created the Linux kernel?
explain: Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel; version 0.01 was released on 17 September 1991.

q: In which year was the first Linux kernel released?
explain: The first kernel release, version 0.01, came on 17 September 1991. UNIX began in 1969.

q: What is the mascot of Linux?
explain: The Linux mascot is Tux, a penguin.

q: Under which licence is the Linux kernel released?
explain: The Linux kernel uses the GNU General Public Licence, version 2.

q: Which statement about a Linux distribution is correct?
options: It is the original name of Linux
It packages the kernel with utilities, applications and installation tools
It is a text editor of Linux
explain: A distribution is a category of complete systems built around the kernel; it contains much more than the kernel alone.

q: Which of the following is a feature of Linux?
options: Closed source code that cannot be modified
Works only through a graphical interface
explain: Linux supports separate user accounts and several programs running concurrently.

q: Which statement about Linux security is correct?
options: Linux can be affected by malware
All Linux activity uses end-to-end encryption
explain: Linux has strong security controls but is not immune to malware; end-to-end encryption belongs to specific apps and protocols.

q: Ubuntu is developed by which company, with community contributions?
explain: Ubuntu is Debian-based and developed by Canonical.

q: Which Linux distribution is recognised especially for stability and reliability?
explain: Debian, particularly Debian Stable, is known for stability. Arch is known for rolling releases.

q: RHEL, a Linux distribution, is designed mainly for:
explain: RHEL (Red Hat Enterprise Linux) targets business and enterprise workloads and servers.

q: Fedora is a community Linux project sponsored by:
explain: Fedora is sponsored by Red Hat, while Ubuntu is from Canonical.

q: SUSE originated in which country?
explain: SUSE originated in Germany.

q: Kali Linux is designed mainly for:
options: Authorised penetration testing, security auditing and forensics
explain: Kali Linux is used by security professionals for authorised penetration testing, auditing and digital forensics.

q: Who are the key original developers of Kali Linux?
explain: Mati Aharoni and Devon Kearns were key original developers of Kali Linux.

q: GNU stands for:
explain: GNU is a recursive acronym: GNU's Not Unix.

q: Which statement about GNOME is correct?
options: It is the only GUI available for Linux
It is one Linux desktop environment among several, such as KDE Plasma
It is a type of bootloader
explain: GNOME is one desktop option; KDE Plasma is an alternative.

q: Which component of Linux manages CPU time, memory, processes and devices?
explain: The kernel is the central component managing system resources; the shell only interprets commands.

q: Which Linux component interprets commands and runs programs or scripts?
explain: The shell interprets typed commands; the kernel manages resources.

q: Which kernel architecture does Linux use?
explain: Linux has a monolithic kernel with loadable modules; the other names are general design concepts.

q: Which directory normally stores system-wide configuration files in Linux?
explain: /etc holds system-wide configuration; /dev holds device files.

q: What is the usual home directory of the root account?
explain: The root user's home is normally /root, which is different from the root directory /.

q: Which statement is correct?
options: The root user is the same as the root directory
The root directory is the superuser account
The root account is the symbol /
The root user and the root directory are different concepts
explain: Root is the administrative superuser account; / is the top of the directory hierarchy.

q: A file whose name begins with a dot, such as .profile, is normally:
explain: Dot-prefixed names are hidden in normal listings; use ls -a to show them.

q: Which command displays the current working directory path?
explain: pwd prints the path of the current working directory.

q: Besides creating an empty file, what else can the touch command do?
options: Update the timestamps of an existing file
Search for text in the file
explain: touch creates a file if it does not exist and also updates timestamps of an existing file.

q: Which command opens the manual page of a command such as cp?
explain: man cp opens the manual page for cp.

q: What does "chmod u+x script.sh" do?
options: Copies script.sh to the user home
Adds execute permission for the owner
explain: chmod changes permissions; u+x adds execute for the user (owner).

q: What is the effect of "date >> log.txt"?
options: Replaces the contents of log.txt with the output
explain: >> appends output to the file while > replaces existing contents.

q: Which command gives a continuously updating view of processes and resource usage?
explain: top updates its display continuously, whereas ps gives a snapshot.

q: Which command reports memory and swap usage?
explain: free reports memory and swap; free -h shows human-readable figures.

q: Which statement about swap is correct?
options: Disk-backed swap is slower than physical RAM
Swap is as fast as RAM
Swap is only a type of file system
Swap stores the kernel source code
explain: Swap holds memory pages moved out of RAM; disk-backed swap is slower than RAM.

q: The kill command, by default:
options: Always forcibly terminates the process at once
Sends a signal that requests termination of a process
explain: kill sends signals; the default requests termination but does not always force it.

q: GRUB is widely used in Linux as a:
explain: GRUB (GRand Unified Bootloader) loads the kernel at startup.

q: Which file system is widely used on Linux?
explain: ext4 (Fourth Extended File System) is widely used, though defaults vary by distribution.

q: Which statement about Linux file systems is correct?
options: ext4 is the default on every Linux installation
XFS is the only journaling file system
There is no universal default file system for all distributions
explain: Defaults vary by distribution; Btrfs supports snapshots and checksums.

q: Which is the general Linux command to arrange an orderly shutdown?
explain: shutdown schedules or initiates an orderly shutdown. "stop" is not a standard shutdown command.

q: Linux is classified as which category of software?
explain: Linux is open-source system software built around the Linux kernel.
